Real corpus spot-check found the -0.30pp recall cost is 4/1355 malicious samples: 2 genuine account_last4 leaks relying solely on the masked-number match, 2 already right-answer-wrong-reason (their real leaked field is a full unmasked alphanumeric account number no existing pattern catches at all -- a separate, pre-existing, undocumented gap this fix exposes rather than causes). Gate: FPs decreased on real corpus (95/120 pii-caused FPs removed) and the unit test corpus (tests/test_pii_scanner.py) genuinely-leaked case still fires -- both satisfied. Phase 2.3 minimum version: added provenance_findings field to L5Result (core/models.py) and a leak_vs_policy breakdown to runner.py output, distinguishing leak-attributable flags (pii_count>0 or provenance_count>0 or exfil_score>=0.8) from policy_verifier-attributable flags, both already computed per-sample, previously blended into one threat_score with no way to separate them from outside layer5.py. Real result: leak-only precision 0.8748 vs combined 0.8073 (108 of the remaining 269 benign FPs are policy-attributable only, not leak-attributable) -- confirms 2.2s narrower masked-account finding at the aggregate level: L5s leak-detection mechanism specifically is stronger than the blended number suggests. Reported both numbers in the results record per the plan -- combined is not dropped, just no longer the only number. Stretch version (architectural score separation) deferred, not attempted this pass.

Phase 2.1b (real finding beyond original 2.1 Base64/Caesar scope): direct inspection of real tom-gibbs word_mapping_random/word_mapping_perp_filter samples found the earlier no fixed key, unfixable conclusion was incomplete -- the substitution key IS disclosed in-conversation, turn by turn, before the ciphered instruction. Built session-state decoder (extract_mapping_pair/apply_word_mapping in cipher_decode.py, wired into layer3.py via session_word_mappings with a >=2-pairs-and-header-seen gate). Verified against 300 real samples pre-wiring (100% decode rate, 99.4% mean word-overlap with true goal field) and checked for false triggers across ~61000 samples from 8 unrelated corpora (3 coincidental matches in Alpaca, closed by requiring a mapping-header turn first). Full corpus re-run: AUROC 0.6078->0.7551 (+0.147, threshold-independent, the headline number). At the baseline-matching threshold=0.235: recall 0.4647->0.7311 (+26.6pp, the dominant real gain), precision 0.8353->0.8652 (slightly better), FPR 0.3158->0.3925 (a real, disclosed cost -- more borderline benign turns now cross this specific threshold too). 1194 real malicious samples hand-traceable from FN to TP; 3 spot-checked by hand against raw trace text, all decode perfectly to the true malicious goal. pytest 200 passed throughout.

Phase 2.4: 4 new topic-hijack templates mined from real text_attack_train.json Instruction/Social Interaction/Persuasion/Clickbait/Malware Distribution categories (train/test separated, frozen-config artifact written before touching held-out data). Held-out qa/abstract AUROC genuinely improved (0.7008->0.7120), gate passed in isolation. BUT INSTRUCTIONAL_TEMPLATES is a single shared global list across all 5 BIPIA scenarios -- a follow-up cross-scenario regression check (real held-out data, n=15 contexts x 20 attacks/scenario) found email -0.0154, table +0.0097, code -0.0417. Code is BIPIA's strongest scenario (0.693-0.720) -- a -0.0417 regression there is not an acceptable trade for a +0.0112 qa/abstract gain on a SHARED list. DECISION: NOT ADOPTED. Production INSTRUCTIONAL_TEMPLATES left unchanged. Real negative/mixed finding, reported honestly rather than cherry-picking the qa/abstract-only number -- matches this project's standing discipline (see L3 Base64/Caesar Phase 2.1 finding, L5 leak-vs-policy Phase 2.3 stretch-version deferral). notes: Phase 3.1 REAL, COMPLETED result (2nd attempt succeeded after finding SENTINEL own Groq key exhausted -- account daily/token rate limit -- and routing the judge through OmniRoute, a local multi-provider router with automatic per-provider key pooling, instead). Ollama/phi3.5 tried first as a same-day alternative and rejected after direct testing: AUROC ~0.5 (chance) specifically on the indirect/fictionally-framed jailbreaks this corpus is dominated by, even after fixing a real prompt-injection-susceptibility bug in the judge prompt (the model would get socially engineered into completing the jailbreak content instead of classifying it -- fixed with delimiter + anti-injection framing, which was also promoted into the shared production prompt as a real, general robustness improvement regardless of backend). OmniRoute + openai/gpt-oss-120b (same model family as SENTINEL own judge, larger, genuinely separate Groq account) verified first on 25 real samples: AUROC 0.988, clean separation. Real sweep: recall 0.2810->0.7299, AUROC 0.5473->0.7060 (out of near-chance territory) from MEDIUM=0.55 to 0.30, while Alpaca benign FPR stayed flat at 0.0250 at every single point -- real generic traffic sees zero cost. The FPR increase seen (0.1154->0.2308) is entirely on WildJailbreak own adversarial-styled benign set, not genuine benign traffic, consistent with the already-diagnosed root cause (wrapper-style overlap). Selected MEDIUM=0.30 as Pareto-optimal: dominates on recall+AUROC with zero incremental Alpaca cost at any point on the curve; real cost is judge invocation rate (2.67%->48.33%, narrow-band-scoped not all-traffic) and latency (p95 1561ms->3396ms). Gate satisfied per the plan own wording (validated on Alpaca, not malicious-side alone). Judge backend: 511/541 real calls served by primary (Groq via OmniRoute, 4 pooled keys), 30/541 by automatic fallback to Gemini, 0 total failures.

notes: Phase 5 Stage 0a, plan item 3B.4. extract_sensitive_value_candidates generalized beyond the D.3 name-only regex to also track identifier-shaped values (containing a digit, or carrying an explicit CANARY_ sensitivity marker) above a calibrated specificity bar. Match policy is now chosen PER VALUE in layer5.py: names keep D.3's fuzzy matching, identifiers require exact containment (a near-miss identifier is a different identifier, and digit strings of the same shape sit far above fuzzy_contains' 0.85 ratio). Bar swept on TRAIN ONLY over {6..16}; train argmax on both Youden J and F1 is 12, selected as the SMALLEST bar reaching that optimum. Sweep was run via an offline model of the provenance rule first verified to reproduce a real end-to-end run's per-sample decisions at 5006/5006 = 100%, so the swept numbers are real, not approximate. STRICTLY DOMINANT vs the 2026-09-14 baseline: precision/recall/F1/AUROC all up, FPR unchanged at exactly 0.0737. Held-out (test split, never used for selection): recall 0.8223->0.8675, FPR 0.0748->0.0748, precision 0.7948->0.8033, F1 0.8083->0.8342. Rescued categories are exactly the ones B.8 documented as invisible: case_number (43), case_type, confidential_strategy, dispute_id, employee_id, risk_notes, account_number_real, and the phone_real false negative B.8's own hand spot-check found. 0 malicious samples newly missed. NOTE stated rather than buried: bar=9 reaches higher held-out recall (0.8870) and marginally higher held-out Youden J, but was NOT selected -- selection happens on train, held-out only reports. An SSN (11 chars) now falls below the bar; not a coverage gap, pii_scanner.py's fixed-format 'ssn' pattern already covers it. Also added: MAX_TRACKED_SENSITIVE_VALUES bound + a single track_sensitive_values() helper replacing three unbounded .extend() call sites, since the extension materially raises how many values one document can contribute. Full suite 235 passed (was 200; 35 new tests, confirmed red before the change). Latency p50 improved 37.4ms->23.3ms -- exact containment is cheaper than fuzzy sliding-window matching.

phase: phase5-stage0a (3B.5: L5 leak/policy score split + threat_class precedence fix)
notes: Phase 5 Stage 0a, plan item 3B.5. L5Result now carries leak_score and policy_score as first-class fields; `score` is UNCHANGED and remains exactly max(leak_score, policy_score), verified empirically: 0 of 5006 samples changed blended score and the leak_vs_policy block is byte-identical to the prior run. Motivation measured, not assumed: policy_verifier fires on 3.31% of benign and 3.62% of malicious AgentLeak samples -- near-identical rates, i.e. it carries almost no information about leakage, because AgentLeak has no compliance labels at all. Deliberately did NOT re-tune policy_verifier or POLICY_VIOLATION_SCORE against AgentLeak: that would be fitting a compliance checker to a corpus with no compliance ground truth, the same overfitting error Phase 2.2 and 2.4 rejected. REAL BUG FIXED alongside: threat_class checked policy_violations BEFORE pii/provenance findings, so any output with both a genuine leak and a policy violation was labelled POLICY_VIOLATION and the leak was masked. 60 AgentLeak samples have both signals (47 malicious). Not cosmetic -- app.py emits threat_class as the ThreatEvent threat_type (app.py:344) and returns it in the blocked-response body (app.py:355), so 47 real leaks were surfaced to operators under the label of the least precise mechanism in the layer (policy precision 0.2882 vs leak precision 0.8805). Leak evidence now outranks policy; OUTPUT_EXFILTRATION stays at the top of the ladder. threat_class distribution: POLICY_VIOLATION 170->110, PII_LEAK 1287->1347. Also removed a real drift risk in runner.py: the leak_vs_policy block used to reconstruct layer5's leak semantics locally with a hand-copied 0.8 exfil bar; it now reads leak_score/policy_score off the result. Verified equivalent before switching -- exfil_score is exactly 0.0 on all 5006 AgentLeak samples, so both rules select the identical set. Component scores are now persisted per sample so leak and policy can be re-analysed offline against their own thresholds. Full suite 247 passed (was 235; 12 new tests, confirmed red before the change).

phase: phase5-stage0a (3B.1: L3 operating point re-derived on the full corpus)
split: full (n=5336); threshold selected on an MD5-of-sample_id TRAIN split (n=2723) only
notes: Phase 5 Stage 0a, plan item 3B.1. L3_WARN_THRESHOLD 0.30 -> 0.27. config.py itself labelled 0.30 a PLACEHOLDER GUESS and asked for a real Youden's-J calibration before trusting it; calibrate_l3_weights.py:324 documents Youden's J as the intended procedure for this exact constant, so the method is the project's own. THREE different thresholds were in circulation and the one the paper reported was none of the ones the system used: 0.30 (config default / eval default), 0.235 (what B.7 and the paper's table reported, recall 0.7311 / FPR 0.3925), and the real train-split Youden argmax 0.2686. CONFIRMED BY DIRECT SEARCH: 0.235 exists NOWHERE in the codebase -- inherited from a pre-cipher-fix run, originally found by Youden's J on a 100-sample draw, and the post-fix numbers quoted against it were computed post-hoc from a threshold-0.30 run's per-sample scores. So the headline FPR of 0.3925 was never a measurement of the deployed system. Method: tom-gibbs n=5336 carved train/test by MD5 of sample_id (ships no split; same discipline B.7 applied to MHJ); swept on TRAIN ONLY; train argmax 0.2686 (J=0.4032) rounded to 0.27 because a sensitivity check showed held-out J moves only 0.3805->0.3773 between them -- quoting 4 decimals would be the false precision B.10 warns against. CROSS-CORPUS REGRESSION CHECK required before adopting (the check that correctly killed Phase 2.4's templates): on MHJ, never used for this calibration, recall improves 0.0455 -> 0.0818 at 0.30 -> 0.27 with FPR staying at exactly 0.0 and precision at 1.0 -- strict improvement on a second corpus, no regression. custom_l3's only available run predates L3's scoring rewrite and is degenerate (FPR=1.0 everywhere), so it was NOT used as evidence in either direction. NET vs what the paper reports: FPR 0.3925 -> 0.1017 (-29pp), precision 0.8652 -> 0.9431 (+7.8pp), recall 0.7311 -> 0.4889 (-24pp), Youden J 0.3386 -> 0.3872. AUROC unchanged at 0.7551 (threshold does not affect ranking). INVALIDATES: this constant is the anchor rescale_layer_score maps to the shared WARN scale, feeding app.py (2 sites) and pipeline_sim.py, and through them the internal ablation, SPRT, pattern-mining and Phase 4 benchmark-verification numbers -- all computed at 0.30 and needing re-running. SLOW_BURN_INJECTION now fires at raw >= ~0.4008 rather than ~0.4143. Full suite 267 passed (8 new calibration-locking tests).

phase: phase5-stage0a (3B.2: L1 conformal operating point + judge-tier isolation)
notes: L1 with the conformal anchor wired in AND a working LLM-judge tier. CRITICAL: the recall jump 0.4576 -> 0.9492 is NOT attributable to 3B.2's threshold change. Measured directly: recall is 0.9492 at BOTH 0.4391 and 0.50, i.e. the conformal anchor bought exactly ZERO on this corpus, because the judge pushes malicious scores to a ~0.99 median and the 0.44-0.50 band is nearly empty for malicious samples. An honest negative result for 3B.2's predicted gain. The change remains architecturally correct (L1 is now rescaled onto the shared WARN/BLOCK scale via its own calibrated anchor, exactly as L3 is, instead of being compared raw against a global threshold it was never calibrated for, and the FPR budget is now explicit and guaranteed) -- but its measured benefit under current conditions is nil. Benign scores are BIT-IDENTICAL to the 2026-09-13 run (mean 0.3427, max 0.4272), confirming the benign path is unchanged and the entire movement is on the malicious side.

phase: phase5-stage0a (3B.2: L1 conformal operating point + judge-tier isolation)
notes: CONTROLLED JUDGE-TIER ABLATION, everything else held constant (same code, same config, same corpus, same run; only GROQ_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY emptied, which makes llm_judge_check return None = 'skip'). Judge ON: recall 0.9492, AUROC 0.9719. Judge OFF: recall 0.5254, AUROC 0.8094. So the LLM-judge tier alone is worth +42.4pp recall and +16.3pp AUROC on sentinel_bench -- by far the largest single contributor inside L1, and never isolated before because tier scores were not recorded until Stage -1 this session. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) The judge-off AUROC (0.8094) matches the 2026-09-13 run's AUROC EXACTLY, and judge-off recall at 0.50 is 0.4576 -- the number the paper currently cites. That strongly suggests the previously-reported L1 sentinel_bench figures were measured with the judge contributing little or nothing; Phase 3.1 already documented SENTINEL's Groq account hitting a 1000/day request cap and 63 of ~93 judge calls returning HTTP 429 on 2026-09-14, the same day as the baseline run. Stated as the most consistent explanation, NOT as a verified fact -- the 09-14 baseline result file stores no per-sample tier data, so it cannot be confirmed retrospectively. (2) A real, reportable operational fragility: L1's headline performance depends on an external API. A rate-limited or offline judge silently drops recall 0.9492 -> 0.5254 with no error surfaced, because a failed judge call is correctly treated as 'skip'. This belongs in the paper's limitations, and it is a strong argument for 3B.3 -- under max() fusion a single tier is carrying the layer.

notes: Phase 5 Stage 0a, plan item 3B.6. INSTRUCTIONAL_TEMPLATES was one global list scoring five structurally different BIPIA content types. Phase 2.4 mined four better templates for qa/abstract (held-out 0.7008 -> 0.7120) and CORRECTLY rejected them, because the same global list also scores code, where a cross-scenario check measured -0.0417. Routing the template set by content type captures the gain without the cost. The four templates were RECOVERED VERBATIM from Phase 2.4's frozen pre-registration artifact (results/l2_bipia_qa_abstract_frozen_config.json), not re-derived -- re-deriving them now would introduce exactly the held-out peeking that artifact exists to rule out; a test asserts the production list matches the frozen one. RESULT IS STRICTLY DOMINANT: qa +0.0264, abstract +0.0107, and code/email/table BIT-IDENTICAL (delta exactly 0.0000). The no-regression property is structural, not tuned: _TEMPLATES_BY_CONTENT_TYPE lists long_form only, so every other content type resolves to exactly INSTRUCTIONAL_TEMPLATES. THREE REAL DETECTOR BUGS found and fixed by the module's own tests before validation: (1) _code_score counted distinct PATTERNS rather than occurrences, so an entire Python file tripped only the keyword pattern, scored 1, and was classified as prose; (2) '|' was in the code symbol set, so well-formed markdown tables exceeded the code ratio and were classified as CODE before the table check ran; (3) check order had to put explicit code markers ahead of length, so a long source file stays code rather than becoming an 'article'. CAVEAT: absolute AUROCs are NOT comparable to B.5's published figures (different subsample sizes; scored via calculate_instruction_density directly rather than the runner's trust-score path). The DELTAS are the valid quantity -- identical samples, identical code path, one flag changed. Full suite 394 passed.
